title: 59th ASEAN Foreign Ministers' Meeting Opens in Cebu — Lazaro Chairs; Maritime Security, South China Sea COC, and Myanmar Top Agenda
detail: The 59th ASEAN Foreign Ministers' Meeting (AMM) opened at the Shangri-La Mactan Resort in Cebu on May 7, 2026 — the first day of substantive proceedings at the 48th ASEAN Leaders' Summit week chaired by the Philippines. Philippine Secretary of Foreign Affairs Ma. Theresa P. Lazaro presided as host-chair. Foreign ministers from all 10 ASEAN member states participated, with key agenda items including: (1) South China Sea maritime security and Code of Conduct (COC) negotiations; (2) Myanmar's political transition following Min Aung Hlaing's formal assumption of the presidency in April 2026; (3) energy and food security in the context of ongoing global supply disruptions; and (4) ASEAN-EU relations, following the inaugural ASEAN-EU Sustainability Summit (May 5). On the COC, ministers reaffirmed commitment to the 2026 timeline for completing text-based negotiations, though analysts and China's own expert Wu Shicun have assessed final signing in 2026 as 'simply not achievable' given unresolved issues on geographic scope, legally binding status, and enforcement mechanisms. The Manila Times reported that maritime security would be the central topic in a summit backdrop that includes the ongoing Balikatan 2026 exercises (closing May 8), the Sandy Cay 1 sovereignty confrontation (May 3–6), and China's counter-signaling naval deployments throughout Balikatan. Myanmar remained the bloc's most politically sensitive procedural question: the post-coup government requested readmission into normal ASEAN political processes following the 5-Point Consensus period. Leaders are expected to endorse an ASEAN Leaders' Declaration on Maritime Cooperation, including formalizing the ASEAN Coast Guard Forum as a permanent sectoral body — a meaningful institutional step for maritime law enforcement coordination — and establishing an ASEAN Maritime Centre in the Philippines. ASEAN leaders convene for the plenary on May 8 at Mactan Expo, Lapu-Lapu City.

media.caption: ASEAN leaders descend on Cebu for 2026 summit — 59th Foreign Ministers' Meeting opens — Philippine News Agency, May 7, 2026

title: ASEAN Leaders Tackle First Charter Amendment Since 2007 — 'Cebu Protocol' to Accommodate Timor-Leste as 11th Member; ASEAN Maritime Centre Proposed for Philippines
detail: The 48th ASEAN Leaders' Summit in Cebu is set to adopt the 'Cebu Protocol to Amend the Charter of ASEAN' — the first amendment to the ASEAN Charter since it was signed in November 2007. Philstar reported the amendment is designed primarily to strengthen ASEAN's institutional framework to accommodate the full integration of Timor-Leste as ASEAN's 11th member, which formally acceded to ASEAN in October 2025 under the Philippines' chairmanship. The Cebu Protocol represents a significant institutional milestone: in nearly two decades since the original charter, ASEAN has resisted treaty-level modifications to preserve bloc consensus. The amendment streamlines integration procedures and updates governance provisions relevant to enlargement. The Summit is also expected to endorse an ASEAN Leaders' Declaration on Maritime Cooperation, a landmark document that would: (1) formally elevate the ASEAN Coast Guard Forum to a recognized sectoral body with a permanent mandate; (2) establish a new ASEAN Maritime Centre to be hosted by the Philippines, positioning Manila as the institutional hub for maritime law enforcement coordination in the region; and (3) reinforce ASEAN's commitment to freedom of navigation and the 1982 UNCLOS as the framework for resolving maritime disputes. The Maritime Centre, if confirmed, would be a direct outgrowth of Philippines' 2026 ASEAN chairmanship theme 'Navigating Our Future, Together' and the surge of Philippine Coast Guard capacity-building under Marcos. Separately, ASEAN foreign ministers were scheduled to formally receive Timor-Leste Prime Minister Xanana Gusmão for a commemorative session marking Timor-Leste's transition to full membership.

media.caption: At Cebu summit, ASEAN leaders tackling first charter change since 2007 — Cebu Protocol to accommodate Timor-Leste as 11th member — Philstar, May 7, 2026
